title: Choose the console's visual world · hand 2 (bolder)
question: Bolder hand, as steered. The deal leads with the split-flap concourse board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Split-Flap Concourse
options.lineage: the rail concourse split-flap board at rush hour
options.thesis: The console as a live concourse board: matte black rows of fixed character cells in white condensed caps, columns that never move, and when the stream changes a row its new state cascades across the cells so the change itself is visible.
options.viewport: Timeline as the board: ruled rows of flap cells (time · kind · detail · state), condensed caps; the uncertain escrow row relit amber and re-flapped to HELD until Mark checked drops it off; live updates cascade per character over the stream; readiness, spend and tasks as steel-framed status boards; the dark theme is the board's home, the light theme inverts to the printed timetable.
options.case: Beats every challenger on both axes: a live event stream feeding time-ranked rows with in-place state changes is exactly this product, and everyone alive has read a concourse board.
options.risk: Cousin to the gate board from the first hand, in mechanical-analog form; split-flap nostalgia (clack noise, flap shading everywhere) is one step from costume, so the cascade marks real change only.

raised.raise: The turn the agent is working right now carries a pale band across its full row, so "working now" reads without a spinner.
An opened detail (raw event, tool calls) takes the whole stage and closes with one gesture, never a cramped inline peek.

options.label: The Acetate Manual
options.lineage: the boxed-software reference manual with punched acetate leaves
options.thesis: The console as the boxed reference manual: saturated section boards under milk acetate, a stepped tab rail down the fore-edge showing each section's extent, and every dead-lettered event arriving as an errata slip in held-out vermilion.
options.viewport: Timeline and Briefing as board-colored tabs on a stepped fore-edge rail; pages in a serif text face with condensed grotesque heads and mono machine voice; the dead-lettered event lies over the page as a vermilion errata slip; state changes move in 90ms two-frame steps, never fades; the dark theme is the same boards under low lamplight.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the tab rail makes each section's extent visible and the errata slip is the dead-letter file exactly; loses audience identification, since the boxed manual is an archivist's object.
options.risk: Layered acetate over saturated boards can drown a working screen in object-craft; one board hue owns one section and vermilion never appears outside errors.

options.label: The Graphite Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels divided by one-pixel seams, syntax-derived accents for state only, and money-dangerous actions given deliberate isolation: outline and disarmed until deliberately focused.
options.viewport: Panels tile and persist: timeline, readiness, spend, tasks each own a panel that updates in place; Freeze spending sits apart from every neighbor, outline-only until armed by deliberate focus; state colors ride as syntax accents; the light theme is the same panel grammar inverted to paper.
options.case: Holds product clarity: persistent panels and focus-gated destructive actions are the money-safety model rendered as chrome; loses audience identification beyond developer habits.
options.risk: This is the category's own canon in a bolder suit; its distinctiveness is discipline, not difference.

options.label: The Yellow Signage
options.thesis: Overhead sign bands for a working page: saturated yellow bands hang over each section and persist while it scrolls, black humanist sans with one message per band, white state pictograms on black squares, money figures at gate-number scale.
options.viewport: Sticky yellow bands crown TIMELINE, READINESS, TASKS and SPEND; one message per band; the attention section's band carries its count in monumental numerals; the environment warning becomes the terminal-wide band; the dark theme is the same signage at night.
options.case: Holds audience identification: everyone has made a connection under these bands; the grammar lends navigation more than record-keeping, so it trails the leader on product clarity.
options.risk: Yellow reserved for wayfinding collides with amber money warnings unless the two palettes are kept strictly separate.

options.label: The Dance Score
options.case: Loses both axes: a choreographer's score is not an operator's world, and duration-shaped blocks fit a dance, not a ledger of marketplace turns.
options.kept: The in-progress beat banded pale across the full staff width.

options.label: The Vertical Feed
options.case: Loses both axes: one turn per viewport destroys the at-a-glance record that monitoring exists for, whatever its pull as a consumer habit.
options.kept: An opened detail takes the whole stage and closes with one gesture.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern ops dashboard, played straight: neutral ground, near-black text, one blue accent, standard cards and tables at Linear/Stripe craft, with a first-class dark mode.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every operator expects: top bar, attention alert, timeline table, sidebar stat cards, executed at full craft in both themes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
